data.narrative:
Grain Weevil is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chad and Ben Johnson, having raised $3.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in robotics and manufacturing, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and yields a $9M implied valuation. Using total capital raised ($3.5M, proxied to $4M) as a baseline, a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding stage produces this result. The Peer-Median method was not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer cohort data—while ten same-sector peers exist broadly, fewer than three comparable datapoints fell within same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters, making a narrow comp analysis unreliable and an all-sector median misleading.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7M (low) to $10M (high), with a median of $9M. This range reflects the single reliable method output, with the bounds representing reasonable variance around stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties include the absence of transaction-level comparables at Grain Weevil's exact stage and tier, reliance on the 2.5x multiplier as a proxy for market step-up patterns, and limited visibility into the company's traction metrics relative to the peer set.
